transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess what’s been bothering me is, um, at work during long sales strategy meetings, I have a really hard time just staying in my seat. I know I’m supposed to, and I’m not trying to be disruptive or anything, but I’ll keep finding reasons to get up—like refilling my water or walking over by the printer for a minute. It’s probably not a huge thing, but it’s been happening enough that I thought maybe I should ask about it.
Do you find yourself feeling restless or needing to move around in other situations, like when you're at home trying to relax or in social settings?

Um, I’m not sure it’s as noticeable at home or socially, honestly. The main thing I’ve really noticed—and what made me come in—is at work, during those long sales strategy meetings. I just keep ending up out of my seat, even though I know I’m supposed to stay put. I’ll tell myself I’m just refilling my water or checking something by the printer, but I think part of it is that I need to move for a minute. Does that make sense?
When you're in these meetings, do you also find it hard to focus on what's being discussed or feel like you're rushing through tasks or thoughts?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t think I’m completely checked out the whole time, but in longer strategy meetings I’ll start off really trying to follow along, and then a few minutes later I realize I’ve been staring at the same slide and I don’t actually know what the last point was.

It happens with client briefs too sometimes—like I’ll read the same paragraph over and over and still not really take it in. It’s a little embarrassing, honestly, because I do want to be on top of things. Does that answer what you mean?

Outside of work meetings, do you ever notice yourself having trouble staying focused or needing to get up and move around during other everyday tasks—like reading, watching something, or listening to someone talk?

I guess… yes, but I notice it most in the work-type stuff. Like in longer strategy meetings, or if I’m reading a client brief, I’ll start out really focused and trying to pay attention. Then after a few minutes I’ll realize I’ve been staring at the same slide or the same paragraph, and I honestly don’t know what the last point was.

It’s not that I’m trying not to listen or anything… it just kind of happens. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you ever noticed these same kinds of focus or restlessness issues in settings that aren't work-related—like when you're reading for fun, watching TV, or listening to someone talk outside of the office?

I think… not as much that I’ve really noticed outside of work, or at least it doesn’t stand out to me the same way.

The clearest example is still those longer strategy meetings or when I’m reading a client brief. I’ll start off genuinely focused, and then after a few minutes I realize I’ve just been looking at the same slide or paragraph and I don’t actually know what the last point was. So… yes, the focus part happens, but I mostly notice it in those work-related situations. Is that helpful?
Looking back, did you have similar issues with staying focused or feeling restless when you were in school or during other activities as a child or teenager?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I didn’t really think of it that way at the time, but looking back it was there pretty early—not just high school.

I remember in elementary school, teachers would write things like I was “bright,” which was nice, but also that I rushed through work or talked out of turn. I’d forget homework sometimes, and my desk was kind of a mess—stuffed with half-finished papers. I guess I always tried to seem like I had it together, so it’s a little embarrassing to say, but yes, I think there were signs back then too.
Outside of work and school, do you notice these focus or restlessness issues in other areas of your life, like at home, during leisure activities, or in personal relationships?

I’m not totally sure, honestly. I don’t think I notice it as clearly at home or socially as I do with work or when I think back to school.

Like, if I’m watching something or talking with someone, I might drift a little, but I’ve always sort of assumed that’s normal or just being tired. I wouldn’t want to overstate it. I guess I’d say it’s not something that feels obvious to me outside those more structured situations. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Can you think of any recent situations at home or during free time when you felt a strong need to get up, move around, or felt physically restless, even if just for a short moment?

Honestly… at home or in free time, I’m having a harder time thinking of a clear example.

The thing that actually made me come in is more at work—like in long sales strategy meetings, I keep finding reasons to get up when I know I’m supposed to stay seated. I’ll say I’m just refilling my water or I’ll walk over by the printer for a second, and it’s not dramatic, but I do feel this need to move. I guess I’ve been telling myself it’s just normal restlessness, but it’s noticeable enough that I brought it up. Does that count for what you mean?
Can you think of any recent situations outside of work, like at home or in your free time, where you found it hard to stay focused or felt a need to get up and move around, even for a short while?

I’m sorry, I still can’t really think of a solid example outside of work.

At home or during free time, if I get up or move around, it feels more like just normal stuff—getting a drink, tidying something, checking my phone—not like this obvious restless feeling. And with focus, I mean, maybe I drift sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it enough that I’d confidently say it’s a problem.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer or make it sound like more than it is. Does that help?
